passage: During the free period in the school library, Vishal leaned over the atlas and whispered, "Promise you won't tell? I'm scared I'll fail the reading test and I don't want anyone to know." Rajni felt a warm flutter; out of everyone, he had picked her. She promised. When Kabir waved from the next table and asked what they were whispering about, Rajni just shrugged and said, "Just a boring map thing." Her shoulders felt heavy afterwards, as if she were carrying a full glass of water. That evening she decided that if Vishal ever seemed truly hurt or in trouble, she would tell the class teacher and explain why. For now, keeping his words safe felt like her job.

qa.q: Where were Rajni and Vishal when he whispered his secret?
qa.a: They were in the school library during the free period, leaning over an atlas.

qa.q: How did Rajni feel about being chosen to hear the secret?
qa.a: Special and responsible: she felt a warm flutter because he had picked her, and afterwards her shoulders felt heavy like she was carrying a full glass of water.

qa.q: What should Rajni do if Vishal's secret ever means he could be hurt?
qa.a: She should tell the class teacher, a trusted adult, and explain to Vishal why she is doing it. 🙂

qa.q: How might Kabir see Rajni's shrug?
qa.a: Kabir only heard about a boring map thing, so Kabir probably sees nothing unusual and does not learn Vishal's secret.

grounding: A friend shares a secret and the child feels special and responsible, keeps it, and plans to tell a trusted adult only if someone could be hurt.

passage:
Wednesday
Today Kamal told me a secret behind the library. He wants to join the kathak class, but he's scared his cousins will laugh. "You're the only one who knows," he said.
I felt special. Also like I was holding something that could break.
At lunch Sonam asked why Kamal was so quiet. I just said, "Dunno."
I've decided: I'll keep it. It's his to tell. If it were something that could hurt him, like someone being mean to him at home, I'd tell a teacher and explain to him why. But this is just his dream.
Maybe I'll go with him to watch the class.
Tenzin

qa.q: Which class does Kamal want to join?
How did Tenzin feel when Kamal shared the secret?
qa.a: Tenzin felt special and trusted, but also responsible, as if holding something that could break.

qa.q: When would Tenzin tell an adult instead of keeping the secret?
qa.a: If the secret meant Kamal could be hurt, Tenzin would tell a teacher and explain why.

qa.q: How might Kamal feel knowing Tenzin kept his secret?
qa.a: Kamal would likely feel safe and trust Tenzin more.

grounding: A friend shares a secret and Tenzin feels special and responsible, keeping it because no one could be hurt.

passage:
On the way back from school, Pankaj whispered to Reena, "Promise not to tell? Tonight after dinner I'm going to swim across the canal. The big boys dared me. It's full because of the rain."
Reena felt a rush of pride that he trusted her. Then a cold feeling. The canal was fast and brown after the rain.
"Pankaj, that's dangerous. I can't keep this one."
"You promised!"
"I know. But you could drown. I'm sorry."
At home she told her mother straight away. Her mother walked to Pankaj's house before dinner and spoke to his father. Pankaj stayed home.
Next day Reena told him, "I told because I care. Not to get you in trouble."

qa.q: What mixed feelings did Reena have when Pankaj told her?
qa.a: She felt proud he trusted her, then scared, because the canal was fast and dangerous.

qa.q: Why was Reena right to break her promise?
qa.a: Pankaj could have been badly hurt, so telling a trusted adult was the caring choice, and she explained why to him.

qa.q: How might Pankaj feel when Reena explains why she told?
qa.a: Pankaj may feel angry at first, but might also see that she did it because she cares.

grounding: A friend tells a girl a secret; she feels trusted but, because he could be hurt, she tells a trusted adult the same day and explains why.
